Limantour, Mexico, 26 August 1899 (catalogue 1461, part): word-code telegram catalogued 'sin traducción'; its contemporary translation is filed as the next two records (CDLIV.1a.1883.38.9927-9928); code checked against a key frozen from three other glossed telegrams of the same code

system.summary: A word code in Spanish dictionary words mixed with clear Spanish: only some words are coded (cotorro = Banco, remero = Presidente, sabio = que, crimenes = Bonos, garlopas abocados = E.U.). Code words keep Spanish endings (jirpeo = indicó, jirpee = indique; impulsarlo = hacerlo, impulsa = hacer). Used by Núñez and Limantour in August 1899 (CDLIV.1a.1883.38.9922, 9926, 9929, 9930).
system.notes: No codebook found. key_frozen.tsv: 90 code words from 9922, 9929 and 9930; key.tsv: the 54 distinct code words of 9926 (one of them the pair garlopas abocados, one the hole ampida); 37 of the 65 code tokens are valued only from the contemporary translation (36) or left open (1). Together the two key files hold 130 distinct code words. Code words are Spanish dictionary words written in ordinary letters.

texts.label: Núñez to Limantour, 26 Aug 1899: loan of the Banco de Londres, Bank of England deposit, printing of the bonds in the U.S.
texts.summary: The President has agreed a loan of 4 millions from the Banco de Londres, paying 2 1/4 on deposits once the Government can dispose of them freely; surplus funds, in an amount Limantour is to name, are to go in gold to the Bank of England (exchange today 23 13/16; at 24 or more cash could be converted here into gold and sent to Camacho to be kept at the English bank), Limantour to say how; Camacho asks authority to have the bonds of the new loan printed in the U.S.; the President asks whether unfinished, unsigned bonds in the U.S. might lead to something like an injunction against Morgan. Please decide.
texts.note: Read through the contemporary translation filed as 9927/9928, which the CEHM record does not mention. 36 code-word values come only from that translation (36 tokens; with the hole ampida, 37 of the 65 code tokens have no key value); 28 are confirmed by the independent frozen key. Words: 43 clear verbatim, 4 numbers, 28 code (frozen key), 36 code (translation only), 1 hole (ampida, blank in the translation too, guess [?depositen]), 2 telegraphed words not rendered (te se). Reading checker clean share: running Spanish 0.50, translation 0.60; the checker counts the numbers and Ud./E.U. as holes. Strict recount (12 Nov 2026 integration): 111 of 119 words (units plus the five supplied words) = 0.933, read in part; the contributor's 0.97 counts the 114 telegram units only.

reading_review.note: The contemporary translation 9928 matches the reading word for word and leaves a blank exactly where ampida stands; all 10 Spanish sentences read as coherent Spanish, one with a hole. Lines L01-L07 and L14-L22 were checked on the scans with no disagreement that affects the reading, and the held-out 28/28 was reproduced from key_frozen.tsv alone.

gaps.detail: Blank in the contemporary translation too; "depositen" or "inviertan" is a guess.
Two telegraphed words with no counterpart in the translation; possibly a transmission error.
Last letters hidden under the pencil docket, the watermark or the edge; values from 9928.
May begin with v, may end in o; neither changes the reading.
